title: Cross-SDK retry jitter tuning, opaque idempotency token format, and retryable-error ontology
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define and standardize opinionated retry/backoff defaults, a compact opaque idempotency token format, and a cross-language retryable-error taxonomy for Redwood client SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). Goal is to provide safe defaults that avoid application-level duplication, reduce accidental double-processing, and make SDKs ergonomically consistent across languages.
background: Multiple engineering teams and early customers have implemented custom retry and idempotency logic with varying results. Differences across SDKs cause confusion: different default backoff shapes, jitter strategies, max-retry counts, and idempotency key semantics. This ticket consolidates field learnings and proposes a single set of defaults plus a minimal idempotency key format and a retryable-error ontology that SDKs can implement consistently.
goals: Specify safe-by-default retry/backoff presets for low-latency and high-throughput workloads
Define an opaque idempotency token format that is stable across SDKs and easy to generate by callers
Create a clear taxonomy of retryable vs non-retryable errors with language mappings (HTTP codes, gRPC codes, network errors)
Provide code examples and sample implementations in Python, TypeScript, and Go
Ship cross-sdk test vectors and a migration guide for existing customers
non_goals: Replacing customer-specific idempotency strategies for complex multi-step transactions
Enforcing a single server-side idempotency store model; this ticket focuses on client ergonomics and conventions
success_metrics: Reduced customer-reported duplicate-processing incidents by 60% on newly instrumented clients
>90% coverage of SDK calls using the new defaults within two release cycles
Latency P95 regression < 3% compared to current SDK defaults for typical interactive calls
acceptance_criteria: Spec document approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Runtime reliability
Reference implementations merged behind feature flags in each SDK repo
Integration tests added covering jitter/backoff behavior, idempotency key propagation, and retryable-error classification
Migration guide + sample change logs prepared for release notes
Benchmarks showing cost/latency tradeoffs for each preset published in the Console docs
proposed_defaults: We recommend three built-in retry profiles exposed as enum/preset: conservative, balanced, and aggressive. Conservative: max_retries=2, base_delay=100ms, multiplier=2.0, full_jitter=true, max_delay=2s. Balanced: max_retries=4, base_delay=75ms, multiplier=2.0, equal_jitter=true, max_delay=4s. Aggressive: max_retries=8, base_delay=25ms, multiplier=1.8, decorrelated_jitter=true, max_delay=8s. Default preset for client instantiation: 'balanced'. SDKs must allow opt-in to disable retries entirely and to set idempotency keys per-request.
idempotency_key_format: Opaque token recommended: hex-encoded 16-byte nonce (32 hex chars) optionally suffixed with a stable client identifier. Rules: generate securely (crypto-random), TTL semantics left to server, SDKs should never include sensitive user data in keys. Example: 'rwinf-<32hex>'. SDKs will implement a helper generate_idempotency_key() and attach it to request headers 'X-RW-Idempotency-Key' by default when a request param 'idempotency=true' is set. Document the expected server behavior as best-effort deduplication (not a transactional guarantee).
error_taxonomy_summary: Retryable errors: 5xx HTTP (except 501/505), 429 (rate limit) with backoff, transient network I/O errors (socket timeouts, connection resets), gRPC UNAVAILABLE, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED when ephemeral. Non-retryable errors: client 4xx that indicate bad request/auth (400/401/403/404/411/422), validation errors, semantic errors from model output validation. Ambiguous: 502/503 should be retried conservatively with increased jitter. SDKs should expose a pluggable classifier so applications can override mapping.
backoff_examples: Conservative profile example: attempts at t=0, 100ms, 300ms (exponential with full jitter)
Balanced profile example: attempts at t=0, ~75-150ms, ~200-400ms, ~600-1200ms, ~1200-2400ms
Aggressive profile example: tighter initial spacing favoring throughput-sensitive workloads; accompanies a warning in docs
language_implementation_notes: Python: provide sync and async helpers; use asyncio.sleep for delays; respect cancellation via asyncio.CancelledError; add a RetryClient wrapper class
TypeScript: provide Promise-based helper and fetch/XHR-compatible wrapper; ensure abort-controller support to propagate cancellation; expose presets as named exports
Go: expose functional options on client.New(); context.Context must cancel retries; use time.Timer with jitter helper; avoid goroutine leaks by canceling timers
implementation_steps: Draft spec and circulate to SDK leads and Runtime team (this doc)
Build reference helper libraries in each SDK repo behind 'opt_in_defaults' feature flag
Create unit + integration tests for classifier and idempotency header handling
Add benchmark harness to measure latency/cost at different token sizes and concurrency levels
Roll out default 'balanced' preset in minor release while gated by telemetry opt-in
Collect telemetry and iterate on presets based on real workloads
migration_plan: SDKs will initially add the feature behind a feature flag referenced in release notes. Migration steps for customers: 1) opt-in via client config to 'balanced' preset, 2) enable idempotency header generation on mutating calls, 3) monitor Console duplicate-processing and latency charts. For users that rely on existing behavior, we will provide clear opt-out flags and a compatibility page.
testing_plan: Unit tests for jitter math, max_retries enforcement, and idempotency header insertion
Lang-agnostic integration test running a synthetic server that returns sequences of transient errors to assert exactly-once or at-most-once semantics as configured
Performance benchmarks across presets at 1k, 5k, and 20k RPS scenarios
Chaos tests simulating sudden network partitions and long tail latencies
rollout_and_benchmarking: Stage rollout: feature-flagged internal SDK release -> dogfood in Redwood infra -> beta customers -> default flip. Publish benchmark results comparing existing defaults versus 'balanced' across latency P50/P95, error recovery rate, and cost-per-token. Add Console dashboard panels for SDK retry rates and idempotency header usage.
